blocks.html:
What to know

  • Water is the solvent of life. Its polarity and hydrogen bonds explain high heat capacity, surface tension, and the hydrophobic effect that folds proteins and forms membranes.
  • pH is a log scale. A change of one pH unit is a tenfold change in hydrogen-ion concentration. Buffers resist that change by pairing a weak acid with its conjugate base.
  • Bicarbonate is the main extracellular buffer. The equilibrium CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻ links breathing, kidney function, and acid–base balance.
  • Bonds set shape and energy. Covalent bonds store chemical energy; ionic, hydrogen, and hydrophobic interactions hold larger structures together and are individually weak enough to be reversible.
  • ATP couples reactions. Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP + Pi releases free energy that drives otherwise unfavorable reactions.

Check

check.question: A patient hyperventilates and blows off CO₂. What happens to blood pH?

options.text: It rises, because less CO₂ means less carbonic acid
It falls, because CO₂ is an acid
It does not change, because bicarbonate is fixed

check.explanation: CO₂ is in equilibrium with carbonic acid. Blowing off CO₂ shifts the equilibrium left, lowering H⁺ and raising pH (respiratory alkalosis).
